job.style: a comparison of two related ideas

response.passage: When we look at the night sky, we see many celestial objects that appear to behave in different ways. Many people assume that stars are smaller than the Sun, but the Sun is actually just a typical star that appears larger because it is much closer to us than other stars. While stars seem to twinkle, planets do not twinkle because they are closer to Earth and appear as steady discs of light. A common confusion is that stars move across the sky from East to West because they revolve around the Earth, but this apparent motion is actually caused by the Earth rotating on its axis from West to East. Furthermore, many people believe that the Moon changes its shape because clouds cover parts of it, but the phases of the Moon occur because we only see the portion of the Moon that reflects sunlight toward us. Finally, some think that shooting stars are actual stars falling from the sky, but these are actually meteors, which are small objects that burn up upon entering our atmosphere. Unlike the Sun, which is a massive star, these meteors are tiny fragments of rock and dust.
response.summary: The Sun is a star that looks large due to its proximity, while other stars appear as twinkling points. The apparent motion of stars and the phases of the Moon are caused by the Earth's rotation and the Moon's reflection of sunlight, respectively.
